description: Verified golden Q&A set for Zantara RAG evaluation. Ground-truth is sourced ONLY from research files committed on origin/main (S6 regulatory captures) and the canonical KBLI 2025 catalog extracted from BPS Reg 7/2025. Each pair carries: the question, a verbatim-grounded ground_truth answer, the must-contain key facts the answer must assert (for generation faithfulness scoring), and the expected_source basenames a correct retrieval should surface (for recall@k). NO NotebookLM live calls — all ground-truth is from committed artifacts (anti-hallucination: every claim is grep-verifiable on this branch).

pairs.question: What is the current KBLI 2025 code for a villa / short-stay accommodation in Bali, and is 55193 or 55203 the right one?
pairs.ground_truth: Under KBLI 2025 (BPS Regulation 7/2025) the current code for direct villa operations is 55203 - AKTIVITAS VILA (TERBUKA, 100% foreign ownership allowed). 55193 is NOT a current KBLI 2025 villa code: it is a legacy KBLI 2020 / PP28 source code that maps to 55203 in KBLI 2025. Final classification still depends on the operating model (direct operation vs third-party management 55901 vs intermediation 55400).

pairs.question: Can a foreigner own 100% of a villa accommodation business (KBLI 55203) in Indonesia?
pairs.ground_truth: Yes. KBLI 55203 (AKTIVITAS VILA) is classified TERBUKA in the KBLI 2025 catalog, meaning 100% foreign ownership (WNA) is allowed via a PT PMA. Licensing is Mikro/Kecil/Menengah: Menengah Rendah, requiring NIB plus Sertifikat Standar.

pairs.question: What is the minimum paid-up capital for a PT PMA in 2025?
pairs.ground_truth: The minimum paid-up capital (modal ditempatkan/disetor) for a PT PMA is IDR 2,500,000,000 (2.5 billion) per company, set by Permen BKPM 5/2025 Pasal 26(10), reduced drastically from the previous IDR 10 billion. There is a 12-month lock-up (Pasal 27(1)): the capital cannot be moved out of the company account for at least 12 months except for asset purchase, building construction, or operational expenses.

pairs.question: What is the minimum total investment value for a PT PMA in 2025?
pairs.ground_truth: The minimum total investment (nilai investasi) must be greater than IDR 10,000,000,000 (10 billion) per 5-digit KBLI code per business location, per PP 28/2025 Pasal 212(2). This excludes land and buildings, except for real-estate/accommodation sectors (e.g. 68111 Real Estate, villa) where land+buildings count toward the threshold. It is 'greater than' 10 billion, not equal to.

pairs.question: Is a nominee arrangement legal for a PT PMA in Indonesia?
pairs.ground_truth: No. Nominee arrangements are prohibited. The ban originates in UU 25/2007 (Penanaman Modal) Pasal 33 and is restated verbatim in Perka BKPM 13/2017 Pasal 12 ayat (6): investors are forbidden from making any agreement or statement that share ownership in a PT is for and on behalf of another person. In Bali, Perda Provinsi Bali 4/2026 criminalizes nominee arrangements.

pairs.question: What is the general principle of the Indonesian Positive Investment List?
pairs.ground_truth: Per Perpres 49/2021 Pasal 2(1) (amending Perpres 10/2021, which abolished the Negative Investment List/DNI), all business fields are open to investment EXCEPT those declared closed (tertutup) or reserved exclusively for the central government. The four effective categories are TERBUKA (100% foreign allowed), TERBATAS (foreign-ownership cap, requires local partner), TERTUTUP (closed to foreigners), and Priority Sectors (incentive-eligible).

pairs.question: What is the effective VAT (PPN) rate in Indonesia for 2025-2026?
pairs.ground_truth: The effective PPN rate for standard goods/services is 11%, derived from PMK 131/2024 using DPP Nilai Lain of 11/12 times the 12% statutory rate. The statutory headline rate is 12% from 2025-01-01 (UU HPP 7/2021), but the full 12% applies only to luxury goods subject to PPnBM (e.g. residences over Rp 30 billion, yachts, jets).

pairs.question: What is the corporate income tax (PPh Badan) rate in Indonesia?
pairs.ground_truth: The standard corporate income tax (PPh Badan) rate for resident corporate taxpayers and permanent establishments (BUT) is 22%, effective from tax year 2022, per UU 7/2021 (HPP). PPh 25 monthly installments are paid at 1/12 of the prior year's tax liability, due by the 15th of the following month.

pairs.question: What is the PPh 23 withholding rate on domestic services and royalties?
pairs.ground_truth: PPh 23 withholding under UU 36/2008 Pasal 23(1) is 15% of the gross amount for dividends, interest, and royalties paid to residents. (A 2% rate applies to certain service fees; an extra 100% surcharge applies if the recipient has no NPWP.)

pairs.question: What system replaced DJP Online for Indonesian tax filing in 2025?
pairs.ground_truth: CoreTax (PSIAP), introduced by PMK 81/2024, definitively replaced the legacy DJP Online system in 2025.

pairs.question: Can a foreigner own freehold land (Hak Milik) in Indonesia?
pairs.ground_truth: No. Hak Milik (freehold) can only be held by Indonesian citizens (WNI) per UU 5/1960 (UUPA) Pasal 21. Foreigners cannot hold Hak Milik directly, and using a nominee to do so is void and a criminal offense.

pairs.question: What is the maximum duration of Hak Pakai (right-to-use) land for a foreigner?
pairs.ground_truth: Hak Pakai has a maximum duration of 80 years, structured as 30 years initial + 20 years extension (perpanjangan) + 30 years renewal (pembaharuan), per Permen ATR/BPN 29/2016. It is the only direct land title available to an individual foreigner (WNA), requires a valid KITAS/KITAP, and is limited to residential use.

pairs.question: Can a PT PMA hold HGB (right-to-build) land for commercial use?
pairs.ground_truth: Yes. HGB (Hak Guna Bangunan) can be held by Indonesian legal entities including a PT PMA (but not by an individual foreigner directly). Its maximum duration is 80 years (30+20+30) and it permits commercial use such as rental villas and hotels.
